definitions.explanation: The person who wrote a particular text, article, or book. Often used in formal or academic contexts to identify the writer of a specific work.

examples.japanese: この{記事|きじ}の{執筆者|しっぴつしゃ}は{不明|ふめい}だ。
examples.english: The author of this article is unknown.

examples.japanese: {執筆者|しっぴつしゃ}の{名前|なまえ}が{論文|ろんぶん}の{末尾|まつび}に{記載|きさい}されている。
examples.english: The author's name is listed at the end of the paper.

examples.japanese: この{辞書|じしょ}は{百人|ひゃくにん}を{超|こ}える{執筆者|しっぴつしゃ}の{協力|きょうりょく}によって{完成|かんせい}した。
examples.english: This dictionary was completed through the cooperation of over a hundred contributors.

notes:
A formal term for the writer or author of a specific piece of writing. More specific than {作家|さっか} (novelist/writer as a profession) because it emphasizes the act of writing a particular work.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {執筆者|しっぴつしゃ}{一覧|いちらん}: list of contributors
- {執筆者|しっぴつしゃ}{紹介|しょうかい}: author introduction
- {執筆者|しっぴつしゃ}{募集|ぼしゅう}: call for writers/contributors

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {著者|ちょしゃ}: author — emphasizes ownership of the work (used on book covers)
- {作家|さっか}: writer, novelist — refers to writing as a profession
- {筆者|ひっしゃ}: writer — used within a text to refer to oneself (the present writer)

FORMS:
{執筆|しっぴつ} (writing, composing) + {者|しゃ} (person)
